experiment: M9: Muon's own recipe (fixed-length step, geometric cooldown) with a SAGA table

protocol.screening: the recipe families are screened like the constant-step references: the geometric cooldown does not depend on the length of the run, so the screening run is a prefix of the full run (the schedule is a one-valued grid parameter, see families.recipe_family)
protocol.accounting: passes = per-sample gradient evaluations / n, initial full gradient of the SAGA table included (1 pass); b + m per iteration with m extra refreshes

definitions.recipe: W <- W - lr_t map(D_t), D_t the SAGA estimator (joint placement; through Nesterov momentum 0.9 when stated), lr_t = lr_0 q^(t b / n) (schedule 'geometric', lr_decay = q), W_0 = 0
definitions.maps: polar = exact polar factor (orth 'svd'); ns5 = five Newton-Schulz steps with eps = 1e-7; frob = M / ||M||_F and sign = coordinatewise sign (gauge-projected for softmax) are controls, not orthogonalizations. lr_0 is a length in the norm of the map: not comparable across maps
definitions.summary: passes to the tolerance over the confirmation seeds: median, min, max, quartiles, number of seeds reaching it ('reached' of 'runs'); a median is infinite when half of the seeds miss
definitions.stop_level: confirmation runs that went on to CONFIRM_STOP x target (stopped == 'stop_dist2'): the runs that stayed on schedule
definitions.edge: grid parameters whose selected value is the smallest ('-') or largest ('+') of its grid
definitions.dist2_over_lr2: ||W_t - W_*||_F^2 / lr_t^2 over the second half (in passes) of the confirmation runs that reached the stop level: min and max over these runs, median width max/min of a run
definitions.compare: per cell of part A: the fastest variant (smallest median, ties broken by the number of seeds reaching the target) among the spectral maps (polar, ns5; with or without Nesterov), among the controls (frob, sign; with or without Nesterov), among the controls without momentum, among the Euclidean references (SAGA, B-SAGA), and their ratios of medians
definitions.part_B: b = 1 cell of part A: results of the two batch-one recipes of part B on the same instance (tuned on the finer grid of q of part B, lr_0 up to 1), and the ratios of their medians to the fastest control of the cell (above 1: the control needs fewer passes)
definitions.law: part C, per run without stop rule: level = median of dist^2 / lr^2 over the records with relative squared distance in [1e-12, 1e-06]; depth_rel_x3 and depth_rel_x10 = relative squared distance of the last record whose ratio is at most 3 (resp. 10) times the level (after a floor or a freeze the ratio grows for good: the law holds down to that distance within that factor; a run that stalls on its floor is still within the factor for a few passes, so these two readings sit next to min_rel); depth_rel_in_range = the same with the largest ratio recorded in the window in place of 3 x level (the distance from which the ratio leaves the range it had on schedule: where the floor starts to show); band = min and max of the ratio over the second half (in passes) of the run up to the x3 record; on_schedule = the run goes below 1e-12; min_rel = lowest relative squared distance recorded (the floor of the run)
definitions.order: part D: rho = factor of lr^2 per pass (q = rho^(1/2)); T = ceil(P n / b) iterations with q^P = 1e-05; lr_0 = 4 ||W_*||_op (1 - q^(b/n)) / (1 - 1e-05) (total step length 4 ||W_*||_op), rounded to 6 digits; C = final dist^2 / lr^2; a seed is on schedule if C <= 100 x the median C of the same cell and scheme at rho_ref; rho_star = smallest rho of the grid with at least 0.8 of the seeds on schedule; rho_star_monotone = the same with the condition at every larger rho of the grid too; fastest = the rho with the smallest median passes to 1e-09 among those where every seed reaches it (passes count the extra refreshes)
definitions.memory_factor: (1 - (b + m) / n)^(n / b): probability that a table entry is not refreshed during one pass, with independent batches of size b and m extra refreshes per step

fixed-length SAGA [polar] b=1.what: fixed-length step of the SAGA estimator, geometric cooldown lr_0 q^passes; map: exact polar factor; no momentum

fixed-length SAGA [ns5 + Nesterov] b=1.what: fixed-length step of the SAGA estimator, geometric cooldown lr_0 q^passes; map: five Newton-Schulz steps (Keller Jordan's routine, eps = 1e-7); Nesterov momentum 0.9 before the map (Muon's recipe)
